(i) a semantic publishing model can be used to provide value added information services to the research community, (ii) a sentence context ontology can be used to convert the research document information into linked data, and (iii) a supervised learning approach based on conditional probabilistic models can be used to identify sentence contexts automatically.

(1) a semantic publishing model is required to publish research content in a machine-understandable format, (2) the Sentence Context Ontol- ogy provides a framework for publishing the research content, and (3) supervised learning techniques are required for automatic identification of contexts in research documents.

a) the proposed semantic publishing model for research documents can be used to provide intelligent information retrieval services, b) the sentence context ontology is an appropriate model to convert the extracted information into machine understandable data, c) the supervised learning experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed model for identifying sentence context, and d) the developed linked data application can be used to support the research community in their information needs.
